nsf:nsf-reu:2547979:
The Physics Department at Washington University in St. Louis (WashU) addresses a fundamental challenge in modern physics education: preparing the next generation of scientists to combine traditional physics understanding with Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods. Through this Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU) site, WashU provides a fully immersive 10-week experience for undergraduate students to perform cutting-edge research in fundamental physics. The participants, selected nationwide with particular focus on students in the Midwestern region, receive stipends, housing, and travel funds to ensure broad accessibility. The program begins with an AI boot camp providing hands-on machine learning training, after which participants join research groups and apply what they learn to analyze large datasets and address realistic physics problems. The REU program benefits society by preparing participants for multiple career paths, developing technical skills that are highly transferable across physics subfields and industries beyond academia.
This REU Site addresses fundamental challenges in modern physics through the innovative application of AI across multiple subfields including astrophysics, nuclear physics, atomic, molecular, and optical physics, condensed matter physics, and biophysics. The program advances the field by unifying physics research through the lens of AI, focusing on three transformative machine learning applications: image segmentation & recognition, time-series or spectral analysis, and reduced models & feature identification. These computational methods tackle crucial research questions ranging from identifying emergent properties in 2D materials and classifying meteorite characteristics to determining exoplanet atmospheric composition, analyzing X-ray emission from black hole binaries, uncovering features of nucleon-nucleon interactions, and reconstructing material magnetization maps. The program's methodological framework represents a significant advancement in physics research, developing machine learning tools that transcend specific subfields and establish a versatile approach applicable to physics and other scientific disciplines.
This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

You’ve invested a lot of time and energy in your education. Now you want the chance to make your mark. We offer challenging opportunities for you to learn and grow professionally. In our programs, you’ll be immersed in a culture of continuous improvement, with the goal of changing health care for the better.
Are you a college student eager to gain real-world experience with a Fortune 6 company that's revolutionizing health care? Join us for a paid 10-week internship where you will be immersed in the fast-paced world of retail management.
Our mission is to become the most consumer-centric health care company, and we are looking for driven, innovative students like you to help make that vision a reality.
Position Summary
As a Retail Management Intern, you will gain hands-on experience leading a retail team, engaging directly with customers, and learning the day-to-day operations of a successful store. Working alongside Store Managers and District Leaders, you will develop leadership skills, learn retail management best practices, and gain exposure to the broader organization through market travel experiences. You will also complete a business-focused project that addresses a real business opportunity and present your findings and recommendations to leadership. Throughout the internship, you will learn how to motivate and manage a store team, analyze business performance, and understand how operational and strategic decisions impact both customer satisfaction and store results.
Retail is a people-focused business, and this internship provides the opportunity to be at the center of the customer experience. You'll support a range of operational activities, including merchandise handling, inventory management, and stocking, while helping the store meet the needs of customers during busy shopping periods, including evenings and weekends. The experience is both rewarding and impactful, giving you the chance to make meaningful contributions while gaining valuable real-world exposure to retail operations.
Education
Candidates must be currently enrolled in an associate or bachelor's degree program
Students should expect to receive their degree (associate or bachelor) between May 2027 and May 2028.
Desired majors are Business Management/Administration, Hospitality, Entrepreneurship, Retail Studies, General Business
Qualifications
Candidates must be available to work 35 hours per week for the full 10-week program on a flexible schedule including days, evenings, and weekends.
1-3 years of customer service experience in a fast-paced work environment such as retail, food service, hospitality etc.
Effective communication, problem solving, and relationship-building skills.
Ability to thrive in a fast paced, customer focused environment
Previous leadership, supervisory, or managerial experience is highly desired.
Must be interested in pursuing a career in retail store management

You’ve invested a lot of time and energy in your education. Now you want the chance to make your mark. We offer challenging opportunities for you to learn and grow professionally. Position Summary:
At CVS Health, we are focused on transforming health care for our customers and making our company a great place to work. We help people navigate the health care system – and their personal health care – by improving access, lowering costs and being a trusted partner for every meaningful moment of health. Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day. Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.
As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.
3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to:
Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
Contributing to positive patient experiences showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security
Delivering additional patient health care services (e.g., immunizations, point-of-care testing, and voluntarily staffing offsite clinics), where allowable by law and supported by required training and certification
Where permissible, the 3rd year Pharmacy Intern may also support immunizations, which includes the following responsibilities:
Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions
Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient
Required Qualifications:
Accepted into, or actively enrolled in, an ACPE accredited college or school of pharmacy
Must possess, or be in the process of obtaining, valid intern and/or technician licensure as required
Essential Functions:
Regular and predictable attendance, including nights and weekends
Ability to complete required training within designated timeframe
Attention and Focus:Ability to concentrate on a task over a period of time
Ability to pivot quickly from one task to another to meet patient and business needs
Ability to confirm prescription information and label accuracy, ensuring patient safety
Customer Service and Team Orientation:Actively look for ways to help people, and do so in a friendly manner
Notice and understand patients’ reactions, and respond appropriately
Communication Skills:Use and understand verbal and written communication to interact with patients and colleagues
Utilize active listening by giving full attention to what others are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times
Mathematical Reasoning:Ability to use math to solve a problem, such as determining the total number of tablets to dispense, day’s supply, and/or number of full bottles and additional bottles needed to fill a prescription
Problem Resolution:Identifying challenging patient or colleague interactions and choosing the best course of action when faced multiple options
Physical Demands:Be mobile and remain upright for extended periods of time
Lift, scan, and bag items
Reach overhead; stretch or reach out with the body, arms, and/or legs to grasp items
Move fingers repetitively; picking, pinching, typing, or otherwise working primarily with fingers rather than whole hand or arm
Extend hand(s) and arm(s) multiple directions to place, move, or lift items
Control precision; quickly adjust machines to exact positions
Stoop to a considerable degree, requiring full use of the lower extremities and back muscles to move items between low and high positions, including bending spine at the waist
Close visual acuity to perform activities such as: transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, reading, visual inspection involving small parts
Occasionally lift of up to 20 lbs and/or exert up to 20 lbs. of force; Frequently lift of up to 10 lbs and/or exert up to 10 lbs. of force; Consistently lift and/or exert a negligible amount of force to move objects.
Express or exchange ideas by means of spoken word where detailed or important spoken instructions must be conveyed accurately
; Have the ability to receive detailed information through oral communication
Any additional tasks as directed by Supervisor or Manager
Preferred Qualifications:
1+ years of related work experience in pharmacy, retail, medical, or customer service setting
Ability to become immunization certified: Once state regulations are met, pharmacy interns should be striving to provide patient immunizations as this is an essential pharmacist function
Ability to work in home store, and across the market in other locations, to meet business needs
Proficiency in Microsoft Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.)
Pay Range
The typical pay range for this role is:
$20.00 - $23.75

Within our Retail locations, we bring this promise to life with heart every day. Our 3rd year Pharmacy Interns play a critical role in supporting our pharmacy teams to consistently deliver on our brand promise, while developing their own skills in preparation for increasing responsibility.
As a 3rd year Pharmacy Intern, you will be focused on applying didactic learning from pharmacy school into real-world practice to become ready for a Pharmacist role. Under the direction of your preceptor, you will complete a comprehensive training roadmap designed to show you first-hand what it’s like to be part of a pharmacy team while gaining an overview of store, district, and regional operations. You will gain valuable hands-on experience through a training roadmap that includes a combination of Key Learning Experiences (KLEs), activities, and time spent with leaders in your district. While in the pharmacy, you will assist the pharmacy team to ensure that pharmacy operations run smoothly, our patients’ prescriptions are filled promptly, safely, and accurately, and we are providing caring service that exceeds patient expectations. You will learn to operate as part of the pharmacy team through consistent application of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), best practices, and effective communication. Throughout your shifts and in all customer and colleague interactions, you will learn to demonstrate empathy and genuine care, and contribute to a safe and inclusive culture where all people feel valued and empowered.
3rd year Pharmacy Interns are responsible for completion of a comprehensive training roadmap, focusing on KLEs that build aptitude in the following areas. As tenure increases, 3rd year Pharmacy Interns take on increasing responsibility of the safety and effectiveness of operations in the pharmacy, including but not limited to:
Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health
Following pharmacy workflow procedures at each pharmacy workstation (i.e., production, pick-up, drive-thru, and drop-off) for safe and accurate prescription fulfillment
Contributing to positive patient experiences showing empathy and genuine care: creating heartfelt and personalized moments while serving patients at pick-up, drive-thru, and over the phone; keeping patients healthy by offering immunizations and other services at the register and over the phone; and demonstrating compassionate care by solving or escalating patient problems
Offering to counsel, fielding medical questions, and soliciting information on a patient’s medical history to provide optimal care, when appropriate under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacist
Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.
Contributing to a high-performing team, embracing a growth mindset, and being receptive to feedback; actively seeking opportunities to expand clinical and technical knowledge needed to better assist patients
Remaining flexible for both scheduling and business needs, while contributing to a safe, inclusive, and engaging team dynamic; voluntarily traveling to stores in the market to work shifts as needed by the business
Understanding and complying with all relevant federal, state, and local laws, regulations, professional standards, and ethical principles. Complying with CVS policies and procedures to ensure patient safety, compliance with controlled substance dispensing and recordkeeping, and to protect patient privacy and security

Completing additional licensure and training requirements, in compliance with state Board of Pharmacy regulations, to obtain Technician Immunizer status to support preparing and administering vaccines
Educating patients about the importance of vaccines and referring patients to the Pharmacist-on-duty for vaccination questions
Monitoring for, and responding to, adverse reactions; reporting adverse reaction events per public health requirements
Reviewing and collecting patient information; tracking and documenting for each applicable patient

Job Description
Are you passionate about workplace transformation, operational excellence, and creating environments where people can do their best work?
As the Workplace and Operational Excellence Program Leader for the Waukesha Campus (Intern/Co-Op) at GE HealthCare, you will join GEHC’s Waukesha Campus transformation program, designed to unify employee experience, customer experience, and campus appeal through modernized workspaces, upgraded amenities, connected collaboration environments, and a more cohesive campus experience.
This role will report directly to the Renaissance Program Leader and GE HealthCare’s Global Workplace and Operational Excellence Leader. You will work alongside professionals responsible for GEHC’s real estate portfolio, capital projects, workplace operations, and facilities excellence, helping coordinate cross-functional workstreams with campus teams, business partners, and suppliers; track readiness activities; monitor program tools and trackers; and contribute to the communications, documentation, and planning needed to support successful openings and long-term operational sustainment.
The Waukesha Campus is undergoing a significant workplace and operational evolution. Renaissance is intended to strengthen the campus as a core destination for colleagues, customers, and stakeholders by creating modern work environments, more connected collaboration spaces, upgraded campus amenities, improved service models, and a coordinated operational roadmap across workplace operations, technology, security, facilities, real estate portfolio priorities, and colleague experience. The program also has the potential to become a leading example for how GEHC defines, measures, manages, and maintains operational excellence across its global real estate portfolio.
A key part of this campus transformation includes partnering with the team standing up GEHC’s first Customer Experience Center, an immersive destination designed to educate stakeholders, strengthen relationships, and showcase GEHC’s devices, digital innovations, workflow solutions, and future roadmap in a patient-centric, visionary, and memorable way.
Key Areas of Impact
Operational Readiness Planning: Support the development and maintenance of readiness plans, program timelines, risks, issues, decisions, and key milestones across workstreams.
Cross-Functional Campus and Supplier Coordination: Work with businesses, enabling functions, project teams, suppliers, vendors, and campus stakeholders to gather inputs, validate needs, identify dependencies, and help ensure each detail is considered before opening renovated spaces.
Progress Tracking & Reporting: Assist with project dashboards, meeting notes, action logs, and follow-up tracking to keep workstreams moving against critical dates.
Program Tracking & Service Optionality Support: Monitor and organize existing program trackers, service assumptions, and good/better/best optionality inputs to help leaders maintain visibility into campus operating model decisions.
Change & Communication Support: Partner with Renaissance Program Team to draft and send clear communications, presentation materials, and engagement updates that help stakeholders understand program priorities and next steps.
Global Real Estate Exposure: Learn how a best-in-class global real estate team supports portfolio strategy, capital project delivery, day-to-day operations, facilities excellence, and workplace experience across a complex enterprise campus environment.
Customer Experience Center Support: Partner with the team advancing GEHC’s first Customer Experience Center and support readiness, coordination, documentation, and stakeholder engagement for this important campus investment.
Operational Excellence Playbook Support: Help document opening readiness practices, sustainment plans, lessons learned, and scalable operating model inputs that can inform an operational excellence playbook for deployment at key GEHC sites globally.
Target Timeframe: Late Fall 2026 - May 2027, part-time ~ 20 hrs a week
Qualifications
We’re looking for students who are ready to learn, contribute, and make a difference in a complex campus transformation environment. You are:
Currently enrolled full-time in an undergraduate program at an accredited college or university.
Ability to travel to the GEHC Waukesha Campus for meetings as needed.
Pursuing a degree in Business, Operations, Facilities Management, Real Estate, Project Management, Communications, Organizational Development, or a related field.
Strong communicator with a collaborative mindset and comfort working across functions.
Organized and detail-oriented, with strong time management skills.
Demonstrates initiative and a self-starter attitude.
Developing proficiency in project management, meeting coordination, action tracking, and status reporting.
Legal authorization to work in the U.S. is required. We do not sponsor employment visas for this role.
Preferred Qualifications
You may stand out if you have:
Prior experience in project coordination, workplace experience, facilities, operations, communications, or transformation initiatives.
Familiarity with Microsoft Teams, Smartsheet, Excel, PowerPoint, Generative AI, or similar collaboration and reporting tools.
Interest in workplace strategy, colleague experience, operational readiness, and continuous improvement.
Proven adaptability and community involvement.
Other Details
Workplace and Operational Excellence Program Support
Support the Renaissance Program Leader and Global Workplace and Operational Excellence Leader in advancing the Waukesha Campus operational readiness roadmap, coordinating across campus businesses, internal teams, and suppliers, and connecting local execution to broader global real estate priorities.
Maintain readiness plans, action trackers, decision logs, risk and issue logs, and program timelines to support consistent execution across workstreams.
Help build and organize the operational framework for how renovated spaces will be opened, managed, maintained, and continuously improved after activation.
Coordinate with workstream leaders, supplier partners, and vendor teams to gather updates, validate milestones, confirm dependencies, and identify escalation needs.
Support weekly program meetings by preparing agendas, capturing notes, tracking follow-ups, and organizing materials for leadership review.
Campus Experience, Program Tracking, and Reporting Support
Monitor and organize existing program trackers, service scope assumptions, and good/better/best optionality inputs to support visibility into FY planning and campus operating model discussions, without owning budget decisions or financial approvals.
Help develop progress reporting dashboards, presentation materials, communication drafts, and stakeholder updates that make program status clear and actionable.
Support research, benchmarking, and documentation related to future-state workplace experience services, colleague-facing amenities, operational processes, and campus readiness.
Partner with cross-functional teams to improve tools, templates, and processes that enable scalable workplace and operational excellence practices.
Gain practical exposure to how global real estate, facilities, projects, operations, and workplace experience teams partner to deliver consistent, scalable, and colleague-centered solutions.
Support coordination activities connected to the Customer Experience Center, including readiness planning, stakeholder updates, documentation, and integration with broader campus transformation workstreams.
Help capture operating model insights, opening readiness practices, sustainment requirements, lessons learned, and repeatable tools from Renaissance that can inform an operational excellence playbook and future global real estate operational penetration planning.

Job Description Summary
GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our purpose is to create a world where healthcare has no limits. Join us to help improve the quality, reliability, and availability of the products that healthcare providers rely on every day.
As a Supplier Quality & Development Engineering Co-Op, you will partner with suppliers and cross-functional teams to improve product quality, reduce supply chain risk, and drive operational excellence across GE HealthCare's Anesthesia and Respiratory Care business. This role offers hands-on experience working with supplier quality, sourcing, engineering, manufacturing, and service teams while supporting medical device products used around the world.
Job Description
Position Description:
The Supplier Quality & Development Engineering Co-op will play an active role in ensuring supplier quality, product reliability, and operational excellence across GE HealthCare's supply base. Working closely with sourcing, engineering, manufacturing, and service teams, this individual will support both strategic improvement initiatives and day-to-day quality operations that directly impact our products and customers. This role provides exposure to supplier management, quality systems, manufacturing operations, data analytics, and continuous improvement within the medical device industry.
Students will have opportunities to work on projects aimed at improving supplier performance, reducing defects, enhancing process efficiency, and supporting supplier development activities. In addition to project-based work, the co-op will support recurring operational responsibilities such as monitoring supplier certifications, maintaining quality metrics and dashboards, and assisting with supplier communications and corrective action follow-up. The role will also encourage the use of data analytics, automation, and digital tools to simplify processes and improve efficiencies of the team.
Successful candidates are comfortable balancing routine responsibilities with improvement opportunities, demonstrate attention to detail, and take initiative to identify and solve problems. This position is well suited for students who enjoy working with data, collaborating across functions, learning new technologies, and driving continuous improvement.
Location: Madison, WI
Basic Qualifications:
Currently enrolled full-time in a Bachelor's degree program at an accredited college or university
Pursuing a degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Business, or a related field
Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including formulas, pivot tables, data analysis, and reporting
Working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Teams, Outlook)
Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills
Strong verbal and written communication skills
Ability to work independently and effectively within cross-functional teams
Available to work a minimum of 28 weeks
Legally authorized to work in the United States
Must be willing to relocate to Madison, WI
Preferred Characteristics:
Prior internship or Co-op in manufacturing, engineering, quality, supply chain, or research experience
Self-starter with strong initiative and a willingness to take ownership of assignments
Demonstrated ability to quickly learn and adapt to new tools, technologies, and business processes
Comfortable asking questions, seeking feedback, and working through ambiguity
Strong attention to detail and organizational skills
Ability to balance recurring operational responsibilities with project-based work
Demonstrated analytical approach to problem solving and continuous improvement
Proven adaptability in challenging situations and changing priorities
Demonstrated leadership skills and community involvement
Experience with Power BI, Power Automate, Power Apps, VBA, SQL, Python, AI tools, or other automation/digitalization technologies
Proven academic performance through strong GPA (3.0+)

At GE HealthCare, we’re building a healthier world - powered by operational excellence. As a Co-op, you’ll gain hands-on experience, mentorship, and exposure to a global organization that values innovation, inclusion, and integrity.

Job Description Summary
GE HealthCare provides transformational medical technologies and services that are shaping a new age of patient care. Our expertise in medical imaging and information technologies, medical diagnostics, life support solutions, patient monitoring systems, performance improvement, drug discovery, and biopharmaceutical manufacturing technologies is helping clinicians around the world re-imagine new ways to predict, diagnose, inform and treat disease, so their patients can live their lives to the fullest.
GE HealthCare Mechanical Engineering Co-ops work on a variety of assignments with responsibilities and hands-on involvement in product design cycles. There will be project-oriented assignments where a manager and mentor are assigned for support. These positions will work primarily with Anesthesia products in our Patient Care Solutions - Life Supporting Systems business segment.
Job Description
Job Summary
The LSS Mechanical Engineering Co-op will support the development and improvement of life supporting products (anesthesia and infant care), focusing on mechanical design, testing, and analysis within a regulated medical device environment. This role provides hands-on experience in the entire product lifecycle, contributing to patient safety and product reliability.
Job Responsibilities
Assist senior engineers in the design, development, and testing of mechanical components and assemblies for LSS products.
Conduct CAD modeling and drafting using industry-standard software (e.g., Creo or equivalent).
Perform mechanical analyses, including stress, thermal, and fluid dynamics simulations, under supervision.
Support the execution of design verification testing, including test fixture design and data collection.
Analyze test data, generate reports, and present findings to engineering teams.
Participate in design reviews and contribute to problem-solving and continuous improvement initiatives.
Assist in the creation and maintenance of engineering documentation, including specifications, drawings, and procedures.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including electrical engineering, manufacturing, and quality assurance.
Basic Qualifications
Demonstrated strong academic performance through relevant coursework, projects, research, leadership experiences, or other academic achievements.
Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's degree program in Mechanical Engineering or Biomedical Engineering (with a mechanical emphasis).
Strong understanding of mechanical engineering principles, including statics, dynamics, mechanics of materials, and thermodynamics.
Familiarity with CAD software (e.g., SolidWorks, Creo).
Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment.
Preferred Qualifications
Strong academic performance, with a preferred GPA of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale.
Proficiency in CAD software and experience with FEA software (e.g., ANSYS, ABAQUS).
Previous co-op or internship experience in a relevant industry (medical devices, aerospace, etc.).

Job Description Summary
looking for a Data Analytics Intern who is curious, detail-oriented, and eager to learn. This is a hands-on opportunity to work with real-world data, collaborate with experienced analysts, and make an impact from day one.
GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. We combine advanced engineering, data science, and clinical expertise to improve patient outcomes and drive operational efficiency. Our devices and solutions generate vast amounts of data—from real-time clinical usage to field performance—and we’re looking for someone who can transform that data into actionable insights that support better care delivery and smarter decision-making.
Job Description
As our Data Analytics Intern, you’ll work on real-world projects that impact how we service devices, support clinicians, and improve patient care. This intern will be motivated, have a positive attitude and be able to function on a team in a fast-paced environment. They should have the ability to self-manage with minimal supervision, to run multiple projects and to provide timely updates. Attention to detail and desire to produce quality work is always required.
The Data Analytics Intern will also work to:
Build interactive Power BI dashboards to visualize device performance, service metrics, and clinical trends.
Analyze data from SQL Server, Excel, and cloud platforms to uncover patterns and drive decisions.
Collaborate with field ops managers, clinical engineers, and data scientists to define KPIs and reporting needs.
Automate reporting workflows using Power Automate and Power Apps.
Present insights to cross-functional teams and contribute to strategic discussions.
Apply AI models to identify patterns in service logs and device usage that signal inefficiencies or potential failures.
Develop predictive tools to optimize technician dispatching, reduce downtime, and improve service response times.
Support the team in ad-hoc data projects and process improvements.
Basic Qualifications
Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Systems, or a related field.
Experience with data warehousing, data preparation, or data gateways
Hands-on experience with Microsoft Business Intelligence Stack (Power BI, SSAS, SSRS, and SSIS), including DAX, Power Query, and dashboard design.
Understanding of JavaScript, CSS, SQL, and other JavaScript libraries
Strong understanding of data visualization, predictive analytics, and machine learning basics.
Proficiency in Python, R, SQL.
Experience with biomedical data, image processing, or web apps preferred.
Desired Characteristics
Problem-Solving Mindset: Ability to break down complex problems into smaller, manageable parts.
Attention to Detail: Accuracy in data handling and interpretation.
Curiosity: Asking the right questions to uncover insights from data.
Communication: Explaining findings clearly to non-technical stakeholders.
Collaboration: Working well in teams, often with engineers, analysts, and business managers.
Adaptability: Willingness to learn new tools and methods quickly.
Business Acumen: Understanding how data impacts business decisions.
Project Management Basics: Ability to manage time and tasks effectively.
What You’ll Get
Real-world experience in a regulated, high-impact industry.
A chance to work on projects that actually help people.
A supportive team that values your ideas and your growth.

GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our purpose is to create a world where healthcare has no limits. Join us to turn ideas into world-changing realities where every voice matters and every difference builds a healthier world. Make a real-world impact through hands-on experience.
Job Description
Are you passionate about electrical engineering and eager to gain hands-on experience in a world-class lab environment? As an Electrical Engineering Co-op at GE HealthCare, you’ll work alongside engineers and technicians on high-impact projects that support the development of cutting-edge CT scanner technologies.
This 12-month co-op is designed to give you exposure to real-world challenges and prepare you for a future career in electrical engineering or product development. You’ll be part of the premium CT hardware engineering team, contributing to solutions that improve quality, reduce costs, and enhance patient care.
As a Co-op, you’ll take on project-based assignments with mentorship and training from experienced engineers. You’ll gain skills in electrical technician work and contribute to initiatives that support innovation and operational excellence. Looking for a well-rounded Electrical technical student that can execute on a variety of tasks on this super-awesome fun-tastic team.
Key Responsibilities
You’ll work on a variety of hands-on tasks, including:
Soldering, assembling prototypes, and building test fixtures
Setting up and running data acquisition equipment for testing
Using electrical test equipment (DMMs, oscilloscopes, power supplies, network analyzers, etc.) to evaluate new designs
Documenting test results and troubleshooting electrical systems
Prototyping, reworking, and designing circuits to improve CT scanner performance
Conducting experiments and diagnostic tests to support root cause analysis
Evaluating software and hardware and implementing improvements
Communicating technical findings to improve system performance and reliability
Supporting the development of engineering, manufacturing, and service documentation
Complying with Environment Health and Safety (EHS) regulations and quality policies
Qualifications
We’re looking for students who are ready to learn, lead, and make a difference. You are:
Currently enrolled full-time in a technical diploma or degree program (pursuing Associate’s or Bachelor’s) in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, Biomedical Engineering, or a related field
Available to work a minimum of 20 hours/week during spring/fall semesters or 40 hours/week during summer
Able to work onsite at our Waukesha, WI facility
Legally authorized to work in the U.S. (we do not sponsor employment visas for this role)
Preferred Qualifications
You may stand out if you have:
Experience in mechanical or electrical trades
Familiarity with Cadence or other ECAD software
Basic understanding of a programming language such as Matlab
Familiarity with digital electronics, switches and/or flux capacitors
Strong communication skills and ability to simplify technical concepts
Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills
Proven leadership and initiative in academic or extracurricular settings
Passion for technology and continuous learning
A cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher (on a 4.0 scale)
Why Join Us?
At GE HealthCare, we’re building a healthier world powered by innovation and collaboration. As an Electrical Engineering Co-op, you’ll gain hands-on experience, mentorship, and exposure to a global organization that values inclusion, integrity, and impact.
We offer competitive compensation and a culture that supports learning, growth, and real-world contributions.

Job Description
About Digital Products
Digital Products owns the definition, development, and delivery of GM’s digital products and the customer experiences delivered through mobile applications, back-office platforms, and connected services. The organization brings together OnStar & Customer Experience Platforms and Digital Vehicle Experience and works closely with Vehicle Products to deliver digital contributors to the vehicle experience.
Digital Products is an exciting place to begin your career because interns can work on real products, services, tools, and experiences that connect customers with GM. You will learn from experienced professionals, collaborate across product and engineering teams, and gain exposure to how digital products are built, tested, launched, and improved.
About the opportunity
Digital Products is looking for Software Engineer Interns and Software Test Engineer Interns who are excited to build reliable digital products and the systems that support them. Depending on the team, you may contribute to application development, automation, data and integration services, software delivery, test tools, or lab and validation infrastructure.
Assignments are connected to real team priorities and may include design, coding, testing, troubleshooting, documentation, and continuous improvement across the development lifecycle.
Potential Team & Areas of Work
Opportunities may be aligned to the following groups and product areas from the Digital Products intern intake:
Consumer Digital Experiences (CDE): Mobile, Vehicle Commerce, Brand Services, and Loyalty
Emerging and Strategic Businesses (ESB): GM Fleet
OnStar Sales, Activation and Experience (OnStar SAE): Carrier & Vehicle Experience Services, Commerce, Global Contact Centers & OnStar Safety, and OnStar AI Engineering
Physical and Virtual Test Platforms: Virtual Test Infrastructure, Virtualization Tools, Vehicle Reflash, Infotainment Lab Operations, HIL simulation integration, and lab operations
Vehicle Software Integrity and Delivery: Calibration Management Tools, Greylock, Wired Programming, and VCAM
Digital Vehicle Experience (DVE): Software engineering and software test opportunities supporting digital vehicle experiences
Potential Skills & Contributions
Build or enhance software features, services, APIs, tools, or automation
Write unit, integration, or end-to-end tests and help improve software quality
Analyze data, investigate defects, and support troubleshooting or root-cause analysis
Contribute to technical designs, requirements, documentation, or delivery plans
Support software delivery, diagnostics, reflash, validation, lab tooling, or test infrastructure
Collaborate with engineers, product managers, designers, analysts, technicians, and business partners
Required Qualifications
Currently pursuing a Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Information Systems, Mechanical Engineering, or related field.
Must have at least one additional quarter/semester of school remaining following the completion of the internship
Availability to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the 12 week summer internship period between May–August or June–September 2027
Coursework, project, club, research, or prior experience demonstrating programming or software development
Ability to communicate clearly, work collaboratively, and learn new technologies
Interest in building reliable, customer-focused digital products
Ability to work onsite at the assigned GM location with the manager and team
Preferred Experience
Candidates are not expected to meet every qualification listed below. Depending on the needs of a specific Digital Product team, a combination of these skills and areas of knowledge may be relevant.
Currently pursuing a Master’s Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Information Systems, Mechanical Engineering, or related field.
Experience with one or more programming languages such as Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, C#, C++, or SQL
Exposure to software testing, automation, APIs, databases, Git, CI/CD, observability, or integration tools
Experience with mobile development, web development, backend services, data engineering, Salesforce, MuleSoft, or test platforms
A class project, personal project, internship, portfolio, or code sample that demonstrates problem-solving
Compensation:
The monthly salary range for this role is $6,400-$10,300 per month.
GM will provide a one-time lump sum taxable stipend payment to eligible students selected for the 2027 Student Program - to help facilitate administration of relocation benefits, please apply using the permanent address you would move from.

Paid US GM Holidays
GM Family First Vehicle Discount Program
Result-based potential for growth within GM
Intern events to network with company leaders and peers

Start dates for this internship role are May 24th and June 14th of 2027.
Assignments will be based on team placement to ensure interns are located with their working team and leader.
Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to their designated work location three times per week, at minimum.

About the Team:
The Automated Driving Production Technology Team develops and improves the production technologies, hardware processes, and analytical capabilities that support automated driving systems. We work across engineering, manufacturing, quality, testing, and operations to improve efficiency, scalability, reliability, and performance.
Our team combines expertise in hardware systems, production technology, data science, artificial intelligence, process engineering, and analytics to deliver data-driven improvements to production processes and engineering productivity.
What You Will Do:
We are hiring an intern to support AI and hardware process efficiency initiatives through data analysis, process optimization, automation, and analytical tool development.
AI and Data Science
Analyze production, quality, equipment, test, and operational data to identify trends, bottlenecks, variation, and improvement opportunities.
Apply statistical analysis, machine learning, anomaly detection, and other AI techniques to support predictive insights and process optimization.
Develop data pipelines, analytical models, and automated workflows for engineering and production teams.
Hardware and Process Efficiency
Evaluate process performance using metrics such as cycle time, throughput, first-pass yield, downtime, capacity utilization, and defect rates.
Support root-cause investigations by connecting process conditions, equipment signals, test results, and quality outcomes.
Measure the impact of process changes and recommend improvements that reduce manual effort, improve throughput, or increase quality.
Analytics and Communication
Create dashboards, reports, and visualizations that support technical and operational decisions.
Document methods, assumptions, findings, and recommendations.
Present results clearly to engineers, technical leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders.

Working toward a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.
Coursework or project experience in Python, SQL, MATLAB, statistics, data visualization, or machine learning.
Able to work full-time, 40 hours per week.

Experience with Python libraries or tools such as pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, or TensorFlow.
Familiarity with Power BI, Tableau, time-series analysis, anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, statistical process control, optimization, or design of experiments.
Basic understanding of manufacturing, hardware development, robotics, automated testing, embedded systems, or production operations.
Must be graduating between December 2027 and June 2028
Intent to return to degree program after the completion of the internship.

The Co-Op position will be assigned to one of the following Industrial Engineering departments: Aircraft Maintenance IE, Air Region IE, Flight Operations IE, Gateway IE, or Fuel Analytics and Sustainability.
Some of the common shared job duties for each department include performing operational observations in the field along with researching data utilized to analyze projects, create procedures, evaluate project proposals, and prepare presentations and reports based on findings. Air Region IE:
Ramp Special projects include evaluating opportunities with technology, new equipment or facility/process redesign to lower labor requirement or improve aircraft arrival time to destination.
Flight Operations IE

Gateway Planning Building and Facilities IE

Artificial intelligence (AI): Create systems and solutions that can perform tasks that normally require human intelligence. These tasks include learning from data, reasoning, problem‑solving, understanding language, recognizing patterns, and making decisions

Commercial Excellence: Developing systems and tools to enable commercial capabilities to serve the customer

Cloud, DevOps & Security: Architecture, Engineering, and Automation professionals focused on developing cloud policy as code, compliance as code, infrastructure as code, and continuous Integration (CI)/Continuous Deployment (CD) product pipelines
Cybersecurity: Combination of people, policies, processes, and technologies employed by an enterprise to protect its cyber assets
Device Engineering: Focused on developing medical-grade intelligent, connected devices and capabilities
Product Manager: Focuses on planning and organizing a project and its resources using Rapid Cycle Model, Market Research, Product Design, Product Lifecycle Management, Product Testing, Requirement Analysis and Concept testing.
Digital (Agile) Mindset: Focus on Business agility, Agile delivery with a fail-fast mindset, and measurable outcomes

Job Description:
Summary:
The Summer College Internship Program is a 10-week paid internship experience that provides undergraduate and graduate students with the opportunity to attend development workshops, network, and be part of our company. Our college interns work on meaningful projects, are mentored under their respective managers, and continue to develop throughout the entire summer. Through the internship program, our interns can attend development workshops that are focused on key business concepts. Interns may work within the skills-based tracks of Business Administration, Information Technology, Actuarial, Human Resources, Analytics & Data, Communications, Finance, Marketing & Sales, Project Management, Clinical Studies, Customer Experience, Digital Operations, and other non-technical and/or technical based degree programs.
This is a paid 10-week summer internship from the first Monday in June to the second Friday in August (up to 40 hours per week).
Interns may reside in either a technical or non-technical area.
Development workshops are provided to help with the transition from school to the corporate environment.
Housing is not provided as part of our program.
Essential Accountabilities:
Specific duties will vary by assignment; specific divisional callouts are listed below.
The intern will be assigned day-to-day responsibilities within the End User Computing team, supporting the deployment, maintenance, and lifecycle management of enterprise software and devices. The primary objective of this internship is to provide hands-on experience with software packaging, application deployment, operating system management, and modern device management technologies while contributing to ongoing team initiatives and projects.
The intern will work closely with senior engineers to learn and assist with the creation, testing, troubleshooting, and deployment of software packages utilizing various installation technologies, including MSI, MSIX, EXE, and vendor-specific installers. Responsibilities will include validating silent installation parameters, create installation and uninstall commands, generating deployment logs, documenting package requirements, and troubleshooting application installation issues in enterprise environments.
A significant portion of the internship will focus on Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager (MECM/SCCM). The intern will gain experience creating and managing device collections, building and configuring software applications, distributing content to distribution points, monitoring deployments, and assisting with application lifecycle management. The intern will also participate in testing and validation activities to ensure successful software deployments across the enterprise.
The internship will also provide exposure to patch and vulnerability management processes. The intern will assist with Microsoft operating system updates, third-party application patching, and Dell BIOS and driver update deployments. Responsibilities may include reviewing vendor release notes, testing updates in non-production environments, monitoring deployment compliance, analyzing deployment results, and helping document remediation actions for failed installations.
In addition, the intern will be introduced to Microsoft Intune and modern endpoint management practices. The intern will learn how applications, configuration profiles, compliance policies, and updates are deployed through Intune. They will assist with packaging and publishing applications, monitoring deployment status, and supporting co-management initiatives between MECM and Intune.
Project work throughout the summer will be aligned with the team's strategy of improving endpoint security, software deployment efficiency, patch compliance, and modern device management capabilities. Potential projects may include application packaging standardization, patch compliance reporting, deployment automation, software inventory analysis, Intune application deployment optimization, and endpoint management process documentation.
Works with a mentor and supports key strategic projects.
Completes work assignments based on business needs, departmental priorities, and individual qualifications.
Performs a mix of technical and/or non-technical tasks that will cover a broad range of business-related projects.
Creates and delivers presentations at completion of internship.
Consistently demonstrates high standards of integrity by supporting the Lifetime Healthcare Companies' mission and values, adhering to the Corporate Code of Conduct, and leading to the Lifetime Way values and beliefs.
Maintain confidentiality and protection of member privacy in accordance with the company policies.
Regular and reliable attendance is expected and required.
Performs other functions as assigned by management.
Minimum Qualifications:
Desired Majors/Degree Programs Include: Computing Sciences & Information Technology (i.e. Computer Science, Software Engineering, IT Networking, Cybersecurity, etc.) or similar program(s)
Preferred (but not required) experience with: Windows 11 Operation System (administration or power user experience), PowerShell Scripting. The ideal intern will have a strong interest in endpoint management, systems administration, software deployment technologies, and automation. While the intern will be expected to learn from experienced team members, we also value fresh perspectives and new ideas. We encourage the intern to share innovative approaches, emerging technologies, and best practices that can contribute to continuous improvement within the team and organization.
High School diploma along with proof of continuous college enrollment (enrolled in a full-time undergraduate or graduate degree program).
Must be in good academic standing.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with ability to interact with technical and non-technical audiences and interface with staff at all levels of the company.
Ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment while maintaining strong attention to detail changing environment and deliver high-quality work product.
Ability to work well in a team establishing good working relationships with peers.
Demonstrates strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving and prioritization skills.
Proactive approach to work, displaying creativity and flexibility in completing assigned tasks.

Job Description
The Future Talent Program features internships that last up to 12 weeks and will include one or more projects. These opportunities in our Research and Development Division can provide you with great development and a chance to see if we are the right company for your long-term goals.
We are seeking a highly motivated intern student to join the Translational Sciences and Outsourcing (TSO) Data Science team within our Pharmacokinetics, Dynamics, Metabolism, and Bioanalytics (PDMB) department. The intern will contribute to the development and rigorous benchmarking of AI/ML methods for pharmacokinetic curve prediction, partnering with scientists to generate insights that support decision-making across drug discovery and development.
The ideal candidate will combine strong machine learning implementation skills with scientific rigor, reproducible research practices, scientific curiosity, and a collaborative mindset, along with an interest in AI, pharmacokinetics, cheminformatics, and computational drug discovery. This internship provides an opportunity to apply modern AI/ML to large-scale pharmaceutical data, learn how computational methods are evaluated in an industrial research setting, and contribute to a reproducible, publication-oriented study with potential impact across the PDMB research portfolio.
Project Overview:
The intern will benchmark existing AI/ML methods for predicting pharmacokinetic concentration-time profiles using a large-scale internal dataset. The project will determine how model choice, data-splitting strategy, chemical similarity, compound novelty, and variation across data sources affect predictive performance and prospective generalization. The work is scoped to produce a rigorous, reproducible benchmark study and, subject to scientific results and internal review, a paper suitable for submission to a peer-reviewed journal or scientific conference.
Primary Responsibilities:
Analyze large-scale pharmacokinetic and molecular datasets and prepare them for reproducible modeling and evaluation.
Implement and benchmark classical machine learning baselines, molecular-structure-based models, and representative time-series or mechanism-informed approaches for pharmacokinetic curve prediction.
Design and compare random, scaffold, time-based, and chemical-similarity-aware evaluation settings, and quantify performance across compound novelty levels to identify data leakage and limitations in prospective generalization.
Collaborate with scientists to interpret results and ensure that benchmark conclusions are scientifically meaningful.
Document methods and results and contribute to a draft manuscript or technical report.
Present project outcomes at the end-of-summer intern symposium.
Required Skills:
PhD student in computational chemistry, cheminformatics, machine learning, computer science, computational biology, statistics, or a related field.
A strong record of publication in top-tier, peer-reviewed scientific journals or machine learning conferences (e.g., ICML, ICLR, NeurIPS).
Strong Python programming skills, with experience using machine learning or deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or similar tools. Experience with model development and evaluation.
Ability to work with complex scientific datasets, build reproducible analysis pipelines, and understand how data leakage and evaluation design affect model generalization.
Demonstrated interest in preparing a publishable computational drug discovery benchmark, with experience in designing comparative studies, building reproducible research workflows, and clearly interpreting and communicating technical results.
Strong communication skills and ability to summarize technical results clearly.
Preferred Skills:
Experience with pharmacokinetics, pharmacometrics, ADMET, or drug discovery.
Familiarity with PK concepts such as concentration–time curves, AUC, Cmax, clearance, half-life, compartment models, and NCA.
Experience with molecular representations and cheminformatics tools, including SMILES, molecular fingerprints, graph neural networks, Chemprop, Uni-Mol, or RDKit; familiarity with molecular property prediction, QSAR, or ADME modeling is beneficial.
Experience with molecular similarity analysis, such as Tanimoto similarity, scaffold splitting, chemical series clustering, or out-of-distribution evaluation.
Experience with time-series modeling, ODE models, neural ODEs, or physics-informed machine learning.
Learning Opportunities:
The intern will gain exposure to:
Pharmacokinetics and its applications in drug discovery.
Machine learning methods for concentration-time curve prediction.
Molecular representations, similarity analysis, chemical clustering, and rigorous benchmark design.
Reproducible research and cross-functional collaboration within a pharmaceutical research organization.
Scientific writing, communication, and presentation skills.
Expected Deliverables:
A reproducible evaluation workflow with documented datasets, train/test splits, model configurations, metrics, and visualizations.
A final presentation summarizing project objectives, methods, results, scientific conclusions, limitations, and recommended next steps.
A draft manuscript describing the scientific question, benchmark design, comparative results, chemical-novelty analyses, limitations, and conclusions, prepared with the project team and subject to internal publication review.

SC Johnson has been leading with purpose for 140 years, building high-quality products and iconic brands found in homes, schools and businesses in virtually every country worldwide – including OFF!®, Raid®, Glade®, Windex®, Scrubbing Bubbles®, Ziploc®, Mrs. Meyer’s Clean Day®, method®, Autan®, Baygon®, Mr Muscle®, Duck®, Lysoform® and more.
The 13,000 people of our global, fifth-generation family company are committed to making the world a better place today and for future generations.
ABOUT THE ROLE
The High School Manufacturing Youth Apprentice will work alongside Production Associates to gain hands-on experience in a manufacturing environment while supporting safe, efficient operations and the production of high-quality products. Through on-the-job and technical training, the Manufacturing Youth Apprentice will develop foundational skills in safety, teamwork, equipment operation, quality, problem-solving, and continuous improvement.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
The High School Youth Apprentice will have responsibilities based on their assigned Youth Apprenticeship pathway:
MANUFACTURING PATHWAY
Train on, set up, and operate low-tech sorting, assembly, packing, and general manufacturing equipment as appropriate and trained.
Follow all safety requirements, standard work, and standard operating procedures, including performing safety checks and properly using safety processes and devices as required and trained.
Participate in required safety activities, including Behavioral Based Safety and risk predictions.
Monitor equipment, identify abnormalities or operating issues, and escalate concerns as appropriate.
Apply basic problem-solving and troubleshooting principles within the scope of training provided.
Support equipment maintenance, including cleaning, inspecting, lubricating, and assisting with autonomous and planned/preventive maintenance activities as trained.
Support efforts to maximize equipment uptime, improve efficiency, and reduce scrap.
Perform quality checks and audits, identify product deviations, and follow established processes to correct or escalate issues as appropriate.
Accurately complete required production, quality, safety, and systems documentation.
Complete assigned technical training requirements within established timeframes.
Maintain a clean and safe work environment in accordance with SC Johnson policies and procedures.
Work collaboratively with team members and cross-functional partners while completing assigned tasks with appropriate supervision and direction.
Demonstrate a willingness to learn, receive feedback, develop new skills, and adapt to various assignments based on business needs and training.
Demonstrate a strong work ethic, attention to detail, and positive contributions to the team in alignment with SC Johnson principles.
MAINTENANCE PATHWAY
Train on, operate, and mechanically or systematically intervene with various types of low-tech packaging equipment as appropriate and trained.
Prepare complete and accurate systems records and apply basic problem-solving principles.
Make appropriate judgments to determine actions needed when direct or indirect intervention is required for equipment settings or equipment malfunctions, within the scope of training provided.
Clean, inspect, and lubricate equipment; identify and correct abnormalities; and assist with autonomous maintenance (AM) and planned maintenance (PM) activities as appropriate and trained.
Follow all safety rules and guidelines and participate in required safety activities, including the Behavioral Based Safety process and risk predictions.
Support the production of quality products by utilizing various tools, testing, and auditing systems to document that products meet or exceed established quality standards.
Work independently with appropriate supervision and collaboratively in both small and large group settings, including participating constructively in team meetings and team-based decision-making.
Demonstrate a willingness and ability to develop new skills, share knowledge with others, and take responsibility for assigned aspects of equipment and operations.
Demonstrate a strong work ethic and attention to detail while contributing positively to the success of the team.
REQUIRED EXPERIENCE YOU’LL BRING
Current high school junior graduating in May/June 2028 and enrolled in a Racine Unified School District high school, St. Catherine’s High School, or Racine Lutheran High School.
On track for high school graduation and eligible to participate in the Wisconsin Department of Workforce Development (DWD) Youth Apprenticeship Program.
Ability to communicate effectively and work collaboratively as part of a team.
Ability to complete assigned work independently with appropriate supervision and direction.
Willingness and ability to learn, solve problems, think critically, and adapt to a variety of tasks and processes.
Process-oriented mindset with strong attention to detail.
PREFERRED EXPERIENCES AND SKILLS
Basic math, measurement, and hand tool skills.
Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, and Excel.
Basic understanding of safety, health, and environmental principles and practices.
Previous technical coursework or training related to mechanical, industrial, manufacturing, or production environments.
Mechanical aptitude.
2.5 GPA or higher preferred.

This role is performed entirely within a manufacturing work environment.
Must be available to participate in the program from June 2027 through June 2028.
Must be available to work 40 hours per week during the summer and approximately 20 hours per week during the school year, with scheduling flexibility based on school requirements.
Must have reliable transportation to and from the work location each scheduled workday.
Must be able to perform the essential functions of the position and tolerate the ergonomic demands of the role. This includes lifting up to 40 pounds and standing, sitting, walking, bending, climbing stairs, kneeling, reaching overhead, pushing, and pulling for the duration of the scheduled workday.
This position is not eligible for remote work or relocation assistance

Together, we are creating a better future – for the planet, for future generations and for every SCJ team member. Join our winning team of Wave Makers and Go Getters and help us write the next chapter in the SCJ story.

Performing testing on new and existing technology.
Assisting engineers with electrical enclosure and test rack creation.
Developing simulators and performing test for customer Protection/Automation systems.

Assisting with Power system studies and SEL relay settings.
Performing research into and testing on new tools and technologies.
Other duties as assigned.

Experience in programming and script files
Practical knowledge of 3-phase power systems

Are able to use MS Windows and serial port terminal emulation software
Have strong writing, documentation, and speaking skills

This position is located in Boise, ID, capital of the gem state, and on the Boise River in the southwestern part of the state. The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
Scope of Work
Resettlement case management interns support IRC’s resettlement team with daily tasks that help welcome and promote the self-sufficiency of refugees, asylees, and other humanitarian immigrants in the Baltimore metropolitan area. As the initial point of contact for newly arrived refugees, the IRC’s case management teams provide support, guidance, and continued integration assistance for up to five years after arrival. Interns will work directly with individual clients and families to assist in delivering resettlement services.
Reports To
Caseworker or Casework Supervisor
Learning Objectives
Learn about the services that refugees, asylees and other humanitarian immigrants are eligible for upon arrival in the U.S., including public benefits in Maryland and local resources in the Baltimore metropolitan area.
Learn about strategies for effective, holistic case management. Develop resourcefulness and problem-solving skills to work independently in different situational contexts.
Learn to communicate effectively with clients across cultures.
Responsibilities
Under the direction of the intern’s supervisor, assist clients remotely or in-person with key services such as housing set-ups, activating EBT cards for food stamps, applying for Social Security cards, or obtaining Maryland ID cards.
Assist clients to coordinate transportation to medical and other required appointments.
In coordination with the resettlement team, conduct remote, office, home or community-based orientation sessions on topics such as opening bank accounts, using EBT cards at grocery stores, or using public transportation throughout Baltimore.
Assist with service documentation through case-notes and case file maintenance.
Other duties as assigned.
Qualifications
Prior experience and interest working with refugees and immigrants preferred.
Prior experience and interest in case management or social work preferred.
Ability to work independently and as a team member in a fast-paced, cross-cultural environment.
Flexible and reliable, with outstanding attention to detail.
Strong problem-solving skills.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) and web-based applications (databases, Box).
Fluency in English required. Bilingual ability in one of the predominant languages of the local client base is desired.
Valid driver’s license, reliable access to a vehicle with current insurance and the ability to travel regularly throughout Baltimore preferred.
Position Details
IN-PERSON: Fall 2026 internships will be hybrid. This includes a combination of standard office environment, remote work, and field time within the greater Baltimore area.
DATES: Internships start with a required orientation on Monday, September 14th (approx. 9:30 AM – 3 PM). Regular weekly hours start the week of September 14th, 2026, and will continue through December 18th, 2026 (14 total weeks).
HOURS: Internships require a minimum of 15 hours per week for 14 weeks. Interns should be able to come to the office at least 3 days per week.

SCOPE OF INTERN WORK:
The Occupational Therapy (OT) program focuses on life skills training in a wide range of areas for self-sufficiency and access to community resources. Kickstart Your Career at Vertex! 
Are you ready to make a real impact? At Vertex, our mission is to tackle serious diseases and to change lives, for the better, for the future. Our aim is to give you the skills, insights, and career guidance to be an important part of that future; to turn your potential into progression. Why Vertex? 
Real Projects: You’ll work on assignments that make a real impact, not just busy work.

Career Launchpad: Build skills, explore career paths, and get guidance for your future career. 
Your Impact
The Vertex Biologics, MSAT Co-Op is a 6-month experiential training program for students currently working towards a undergraduate degree or advanced degree in chemical engineering, biochemical engineering, data science, statistics, biology, chemistry, or other related fields. If you are passionate, collaborative, and growth-minded, a co-op at Vertex will help you gain meaningful experience in our PD Media Development functional areas and serve as a launchpad for your career.
The application deadline for this co-op is November 15th. Please note that Vertex reviews applications on a rolling basis and reserves the right to close this job posting prior to the listed deadline. Applicants can expect to receive an update about their application before or shortly after the application deadline.
Ready to apply? Submit your application and let’s turn possibilities into reality! 
 What you will be doing: 
Vertex is a global biotechnology company focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing innovative medicines for people with serious diseases. The Biologics Manufacturing Science and Technology (Biologics MSAT) group provides technical and analytical support for biologics products across commercialization and manufacturing. The co-op will support data analytics workstreams that improve process understanding, manufacturing performance monitoring, and data-driven decision making.

The co-op will work within Biologics MSAT and with cross-functional partners on data analytics projects supporting biologics manufacturing and commercialization.
Compile, clean, organize, and analyze manufacturing, process, and product quality data from multiple sources.
Develop repeatable data workflows, dashboards, visualizations, and statistical summaries to support process monitoring and technical investigations.
Perform trend analyses to identify process variability, emerging signals, and opportunities for improvement.
Support the development and maintenance of data analytics tools and standardized reporting approaches for Biologics MSAT.
Document analytical methods, assumptions, data sources, and conclusions in a clear and traceable manner.
Collaborate with Biologics MSAT, Manufacturing, Quality, Process Development, and other cross-functional partners to translate technical questions into analytical workplans and communicate results

Education: Pursuing a BS or MS in chemical engineering, biochemical engineering, data science, statistics, biology, chemistry, or a related discipline
Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills
Experience working with data in Microsoft Excel; exposure to statistical or visualization tools such as JMP, Minitab, Power BI, Python, or R is preferred
Ability to organize, clean, analyze, and clearly present complex datasets
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills
Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to self-direct and manage individual project deliverables
Strong work ethic and eagerness to learn new tools, processes, and technical concepts
Legal authorization to work in the United States, now and in the future. Please note that Vertex does not provide sponsorship for internships/co-ops or entry level roles within this part of the organization.

As the biggest player in the game, we trust our associates to innovate the future of supply chain & transportation!
About our Teams:
Transportation - The Transportation team implements business processes and improvement strategies to stay current on supply chain and replenishment processes and procedures. As the largest grocer, ensuring our stores have items like food on hand and delivering it to our customers to feed their families is an important role. This is among many ways the team makes a difference in times of need, including helping provide Emergency relief during National Emergencies.
About Our Program:
Each summer, we select the best and brightest to look under the hood of the world’s largest retailer at our Walmart across multiple locations. During the 11-week program, our interns work directly with teams who are changing the way the world shops. This is the beginning of what could be an exciting career with Walmart!

Direct access to leadership across the enterprise
Executive-led speaker sessions with insightful Q&A
Community outreach events
Networking and social events
Learning & development opportunities targeting both hard and soft skills
Deep dives into different areas of our business
Time management and leadership development as a full-time associate
Compensation and housing assistance provided
Roles and Responsibilities:
Join a team of world-class Supply Chain Area Managers. If you like to communicate and collaborate, then being an Area Manager Intern is the role for you! Area Managers wear two hats: a Leader and a Project Manager. It’s a hands-on, fast paced role and as a change agent and process pro, you’ll be on the front lines of an ever-changing industry.
